$schema: Hand-written token descriptions. Keys are CSS custom property names; values are plain strings, per the DTCG $description spec. Only tokens whose purpose is not evident from their name belong here — the component tier is described by template at export time (scripts/token-export-1.5.cjs), so adding 1,100 near-identical lines here would create a maintenance burden with no reader. Run `npm run tokens:1.5` after editing.
--alias-color-text-primary: Default text colour. Use for body copy and anything the reader is meant to actually read.
--alias-color-text-secondary: Supporting text that sits alongside primary content — helper text, metadata, timestamps. Still fully legible, just lower in the hierarchy.
--alias-color-text-tertiary: Third-level text. Use sparingly; if three levels of text hierarchy are not clearly distinguishable in context, the layout is doing too much.
--alias-color-text-subtle: The quietest readable text. Placeholder-adjacent content such as counts, units, and inline hints.
--alias-color-text-disabled: Text in a disabled control. Deliberately fails normal contrast expectations to signal non-interactivity — never use it for content the user needs to read.
--alias-color-text-inverse: Text on a dark or saturated surface, such as a primary button or brand banner.
--alias-color-text-brand: Text that carries brand identity — a link, a brand wordmark, an active nav label. Not for body copy.
--alias-color-background-primary: The base canvas. Most of the interface sits on this.
--alias-color-background-secondary: A raised or grouped surface — cards, panels, the assistant's message bubble. Warm off-white rather than grey, so it reads as a surface rather than a shadow.
--alias-color-background-tertiary: The third surface level, for nested groupings and inset areas. Rarely needed; reach for spacing or a border before a third fill.
--alias-color-background-brand: The single accent fill. Reserved for the one primary action in a view and for active states — its scarcity is what makes it read as important.
--alias-color-background-brand-dark: The pressed and hovered form of the brand fill. Darker rather than lighter, so the control appears to recede under the cursor.
--alias-color-background-hover: Hover wash for otherwise unfilled interactive rows and menu items. Tinted toward the brand hue so hover feels connected to the accent rather than a generic grey.
--alias-color-border-default: The standard hairline between regions. Should be visible without being the first thing the eye lands on.
--alias-color-border-active: Border for a focused or selected control. Carries the brand hue so focus is unmistakably intentional.
--alias-color-border-disabled: Border on a disabled control. Lower contrast than default, matching the muted fill it accompanies.
--alias-color-border-brand: Brand-coloured border for outlined controls that need brand emphasis without a brand fill.
--alias-color-border-success: Border on a success surface. Never the only signal — pair with an icon and text.
--alias-color-border-info: Border on an informational surface. Never the only signal — pair with an icon and text.
--alias-color-border-error: Border on an error surface or invalid field. Never the only signal — pair with an icon and an actionable message.
--alias-color-border-warning: Border on a warning surface. Never the only signal — pair with an icon and text.
--alias-color-icon-primary: Default icon colour. Slightly lighter than primary text, because icon strokes read heavier than glyphs at the same value.
--alias-color-icon-secondary: Supporting icons — decorative affordances, inactive toolbar items.
--alias-color-icon-brand: Icon carrying brand emphasis, such as an active nav item or a brand-marked action.
--alias-color-feedback-success-fg: Text and icon colour on a success surface. Dark enough to meet contrast against the matching background token.
--alias-color-feedback-success-bg: Background for a success message. Pale enough that foreground text remains the dominant element.
--alias-color-feedback-success-border: Border for a success surface, mid-ramp so it separates the surface without competing with its text.
--alias-color-feedback-info-fg: Text and icon colour on an informational surface.
--alias-color-feedback-info-bg: Background for an informational message. Use for context and explanation, not for anything the user must act on.
--alias-color-feedback-warning-fg: Text and icon colour on a warning surface.
--alias-color-feedback-warning-bg: Background for a warning — something that needs attention but is not yet a failure.
--alias-color-feedback-error-fg: Text and icon colour on an error surface.
--alias-color-feedback-error-bg: Background for an error message. Reserve for actual failures; overuse trains people to ignore it.
--alias-color-feedback-error-border: Border for an error surface or invalid field.
--alias-color-overlay-default: Scrim behind modals and sheets. Neutral black rather than a tinted neutral, because a warm scrim shifts the hue of the content beneath it.
--alias-spacing-inline-xs: Tightest horizontal gap — between an icon and its label, or between adjacent inline tags.
--alias-spacing-inline-sm: Standard horizontal gap between related inline elements.
--alias-spacing-inline-md: Horizontal gap between distinct inline groups, such as two button clusters in a toolbar.
--alias-spacing-stack-xs: Tightest vertical rhythm — a label sitting directly above its input.
--alias-spacing-stack-sm: Vertical gap between closely related stacked elements, such as an input and its helper text.
--alias-spacing-stack-md: Standard vertical gap between form fields and stacked content blocks.
--alias-spacing-stack-lg: Vertical gap between distinct groups within a section.
--alias-spacing-padding-xs: Internal padding for compact controls — small badges, dense table cells.
--alias-spacing-padding-sm: Internal padding for standard controls such as inputs and buttons.
--alias-spacing-padding-md: Internal padding for containers — cards, dialogs, panels.
--alias-spacing-padding-lg: Generous internal padding for prominent surfaces where breathing room is the point.
--alias-spacing-section-md: Vertical separation between sections of a page.
--alias-spacing-section-lg: Vertical separation between major sections that should read as distinct areas.
--alias-spacing-page-lg: Page-level margin for wide or editorial layouts.
--alias-radius-xs: Sharpest radius. For small elements where a larger curve would look bulbous — checkboxes, tight tags.
--alias-radius-md: The default radius. Buttons, inputs, and most controls use this.
--alias-radius-lg: Larger radius for containers — cards, panels, popovers.
--alias-radius-xl: Softest rectangular radius, for large surfaces such as modals.
--alias-radius-full: Fully round. Pills, avatars, toggle thumbs. A large constant rather than 50%, so it stays a pill on any aspect ratio.
--alias-elevation-none: No shadow. An explicit token rather than omitting the property, so a component can flatten a surface that would otherwise inherit elevation.
--alias-elevation-1: Barely-there lift. Hover on an otherwise flat card.
--alias-elevation-2: Resting elevation for cards and raised surfaces.
--alias-elevation-3: Dropdowns, popovers, and menus — floating above content but anchored to a trigger.
--alias-elevation-4: High elevation for detached floating surfaces.
--alias-elevation-5: Maximum elevation, for modals and sheets that sit above a scrim.
--alias-elevation-md: Alias of elevation-3, kept for components that describe elevation by size rather than by level.
--alias-motion-easing-default: Standard easing. Decelerating, so movement arrives gently rather than stopping dead.
--alias-motion-easing-fade: Symmetric easing for opacity changes, where there is no sense of physical arrival to soften.
--alias-motion-easing-spring: Slight overshoot, for elements that should feel physical — a toggle thumb, a drawer catching.
--alias-motion-transition-fast: Quick transition for immediate feedback such as hover. Fast enough to feel instant while still smoothing the change.
--alias-motion-transition-normal: The default transition. Use unless there is a reason not to.
--alias-motion-transition-slow: Deliberate transition for larger movements — a panel opening, a layout shift the user should be able to follow.
--alias-motion-transition-fade: Transition for opacity-only changes, paired with the fade easing curve.
--alias-motion-transition-spring: Transition with overshoot, for controls that benefit from feeling physical.
--alias-focus-ring: The complete focus indicator. Applied on focus-visible so it appears for keyboard users without following the mouse.
--alias-focus-ring-width: Thickness of the focus ring. Wide enough to be unmissable at a glance, which is the entire job of a focus indicator.
--alias-focus-ring-color: Focus ring colour. Carries the brand hue so focus reads as deliberate rather than as an error.
--alias-focus-ring-offset: Gap between the control and its focus ring, so the ring stays legible against the control's own border.
--base-color-overlay-scrim: Raw scrim value. Black at 50% — a tinted neutral would shift the hue of content beneath it.
--base-radius-full: Raw fully-round value. A large constant rather than a percentage, so it pills a rectangle of any aspect ratio instead of ellipsing it.
--base-duration-instant: Zero duration. Use to disable a transition explicitly rather than omitting the property.
--base-duration-fast: Fast — hover and other immediate feedback.
--base-duration-normal: The default duration for most state changes.
--base-duration-slow: Slow, for movements large enough that the eye needs to track them.
--base-duration-slower: Slowest. Reserve for entrances of large surfaces; anything routine at this speed feels sluggish.
--base-easing-linear: Constant speed. Correct for continuous motion such as a spinner, wrong for anything that starts and stops.
--base-easing-ease-in: Accelerating. For elements leaving the screen.
--base-easing-ease-out: Decelerating. For elements entering — they arrive rather than stop.
--base-easing-ease-in-out: Symmetric. For elements that move from one place to another and stay on screen throughout.
--base-easing-spring: Overshoots slightly before settling, giving movement a sense of weight.
--base-border-width: The standard hairline width used throughout the system.
--base-border-style: The standard border style. Solid everywhere; dashed and dotted borders are not part of the visual language.
